thread:
Rina Kobayashi: seeing repeat OOMs on L40S runners in the workload-matrix long-context bucket. Failing ~3-5 mins into the run (streaming + non-streaming). This is on baseline runtime + current L40S preset draft.

Rina Kobayashi: snippet from the job log:
```
E1119 14:18:03.912 runtime/kv_cache.cc:441] cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
E1119 14:18:03.912 runtime/kv_cache.cc:442] KV allocate failed. requested_bytes=1288490188 (1.20GiB)
E1119 14:18:03.912 runtime/model_runner.cc:219] aborting request: OOM in kv-cache grow
I1119 14:18:03.912 runtime/mem.cc:88] device=0 total=48.0GiB free=0.4GiB reserved=46.9GiB
I1119 14:18:03.913 runtime/scheduler.cc:1057] inflight=22 queue=64 prefill_active=8 decode_active=14
```

Claire Dubois: which workload config exactly? long-context = 16k/32k prompts? and what model family?

Rina Kobayashi: this repros in matrix row `long_ctx_chat_streaming`:
- model: llama-3.1-70b-int8 (our standard pack)
- prompt len bucket: p50 ~14k, p95 ~28k
- max_new_tokens: 512
- concurrency target: 24
- streaming: on
Runner is L40S 48GB (pci-e) in the perf-lab pool.

Samir Qureshi: yeah that inflight=22 with p95 prompt 28k is gonna explode KV on L40S. H100 had slack; L40S doesn’t.

Omar El-Sayed: what are we currently setting for KV cache? do we preallocate to max sequence? or on-demand grow? the log says “grow” but reserved is basically the whole card.

Rina Kobayashi: from effective config dump (what the runner printed):
```
kv_cache:
  enabled: true
  paging: true
  init_blocks: 8192
  max_blocks: 65536
  block_size_tokens: 16
  grow_policy: aggressive
  budget:
    mode: auto
    target_gpu_mem_fraction: 0.78
```
(and scheduler)
```
scheduler:
  max_inflight_requests: 32
  max_queue_depth: 64
  prefill_max_concurrency: 10
  decode_max_concurrency: 24
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
```

Samir Qureshi: 0.78 on a 48GB L40S is too optimistic, esp with fragmentation + model weights + activation peaks during prefill. also paging doesn’t save you if you still allow max_blocks to run wild.

Lena Fischer: +1. also prefill_max_concurrency=10 is high for long prompts. prefill spikes temp mem.

Marcus Reed: can we confirm it’s fragmentation vs just “budget too high”? reserved=46.9GiB suggests allocator has gobbled it. do we have the allocator stats lines?

Rina Kobayashi: there are a couple more lines earlier:
```
I1119 14:16:55.100 runtime/mem.cc:131] cudaMallocAsync pool: reserved=44.2GiB used=41.7GiB free_in_pool=2.5GiB
I1119 14:16:55.101 runtime/mem.cc:140] largest_free_block=612MiB
```
then a big prefill batch comes in and it tries to grow KV by ~1.2GiB and dies.

Samir Qureshi: largest_free_block 612MiB -> yup fragmentation + grow size. classic.

Omar El-Sayed: proposed guardrail for L40S profile pack:
- cap kv budget fraction lower (0.55-0.60)
- cap max_blocks so worst-case can’t exceed budget even if auto tries
- change grow_policy from aggressive -> incremental (smaller chunk grows)
Also we should clamp prefill concurrency when avg prompt len > threshold.

Sofia Ivanova: scheduler side: we can set a “long-context mode” heuristic that flips when `p50_prompt_tokens` estimate > e.g. 4k. then:
- prefill_max_concurrency: 4
- max_inflight_requests: 16
- max_batch_tokens: 4096 (or make it depend on prompt len bucket)
It’ll reduce throughput but avoids pagefault storms + OOM.

Claire Dubois: careful on the benchmark matrix though — if we lower concurrency too much, we’ll shift the curve a lot. But better than hard failing. We can annotate as “L40S longctx envelope”.

Kira Volkov: for perf-canary: can we add an explicit gate “OOM rate must be 0” for L40S longctx rows. right now the job just fails and we treat it as infra flake sometimes.

Keiko Yamamoto: from infra side, L40S nodes in that pool aren’t homogeneous on driver minor versions. but this looks like runtime config, not driver. still, we should set the profile to be robust across small variance.

Marcus Reed: +1 on incremental grows. do we have a knob for grow chunk size? if not, we can add `kv_cache.grow_step_blocks` default per profile.

Omar El-Sayed: there’s an internal knob in the KV allocator, not exposed in profile schema yet. we can promote it as:
`kv_cache.grow_step_blocks` (default 2048 right now). for L40S set 256 or 512.

Samir Qureshi: and also consider setting `kv_cache.max_contiguous_alloc_mb` guardrail. if allocator can’t get a contiguous block >= X, we should stop growing KV and backpressure (or shed) before we crash.

Lena Fischer: we can do backpressure by lowering admit rate when free_in_pool < threshold. do we already have a “memory pressure” signal to scheduler?

Marcus Reed: we have `mem_pressure=low/med/high` from the allocator stats (added last quarter). scheduler can react to “high” by:
- stop increasing decode batch
- temporarily reject new prefill
Right now it’s only logged, not wired. Might be too big for this thread, but for L40S profile pack it’s relevant.

Rina Kobayashi: can we get a quick config-only mitigation for the matrix runs today? I can re-run once we agree on knobs.

Samir Qureshi: config-only mitigation suggestion (for runner overrides):
- `kv_cache.budget.target_gpu_mem_fraction=0.58`
- `kv_cache.max_blocks=32768`
- `kv_cache.grow_policy=incremental`
- `scheduler.prefill_max_concurrency=4`
- `scheduler.max_inflight_requests=16`
- `scheduler.max_batch_tokens=4096`
Should keep us under budget even for 28k prompts.

Sofia Ivanova: I’d also drop `decode_max_concurrency` a bit (24 -> 16) for L40S longctx. decode itself isn’t huge but inflight drives KV footprint.

Claire Dubois: makes sense. note in the report: “L40S longctx tuned for stability; throughput comparisons should be within that envelope.”

Kira Volkov: if you re-run with those, can you paste the resulting p95 latency + tps deltas? I want to set a canary expectation (even a loose band).

Rina Kobayashi: yep. I’ll rerun `long_ctx_chat_streaming` and `long_ctx_chat_nonstream` with the override. will post numbers.

Keiko Yamamoto: also, please capture the GPU mem traces if possible. we’ve seen a couple cases where memory spikes during prefill due to temporary buffers.

Omar El-Sayed: action items I’m taking from this thread for the profile pack:
1) L40S profile: lower kv budget + cap blocks + incremental grow step.
2) L40S scheduler preset: longctx-safe defaults (prefill concurrency + inflight clamp).
3) Consider adding schema keys for `kv_cache.grow_step_blocks` + maybe `kv_cache.max_contiguous_alloc_mb`.

Marcus Reed: I’ll check if `max_contiguous_alloc_mb` is feasible without destabilizing other SKUs. If not, we can at least log “largest_free_block” and stop KV growth when requested > largest.

Samir Qureshi: +1. “fail closed” with backpressure vs crash.

Rina Kobayashi: ok applying runner override now. command:
```
benchctl run-matrix \
  --sku l40s \
  --row long_ctx_chat_streaming \
  --set kv_cache.budget.target_gpu_mem_fraction=0.58 \
  --set kv_cache.max_blocks=32768 \
  --set kv_cache.grow_policy=incremental \
  --set scheduler.max_inflight_requests=16 \
  --set scheduler.prefill_max_concurrency=4 \
  --set scheduler.decode_max_concurrency=16 \
  --set scheduler.max_batch_tokens=4096
```
Will update when it finishes.

Kira Volkov: :thumbsup: also please note whether OOM disappears but retry rate increases (some other failure mode).

Claire Dubois: and if the curve tanks, we can adjust the matrix so L40S longctx uses lower concurrency targets. Better to be explicit.

Rina Kobayashi: update: run completed (no OOM). quick summary:
- streaming row: tokens/sec -18% vs baseline, p95 latency +9% (but baseline was “crash after 3-5 min” so…)
- non-streaming row: tokens/sec -12%, p95 +6%
Allocator stats at steady-state: reserved ~41GiB, largest_free_block ~2.1GiB. no big fragmentation cliff.

Sofia Ivanova: those deltas are acceptable for “stable longctx”. We should document that L40S profile prioritizes stability over max throughput in that envelope.

Samir Qureshi: great. let’s bake those into the L40S tuned profile reference. For shorter contexts we can have a less conservative mode.

Omar El-Sayed: I’ll draft the L40S memory guardrails section with these defaults + rationale (fragmentation, largest_free_block). will ping for review.

Keiko Yamamoto: once it’s in the profile pack, infra can set the L40S pools to default to “balanced/stable” and allow opt-in to throughput mode behind a flag.

Kira Volkov: I’ll open a note for perf-canary: add a panel + alert for `largest_free_block` trending down + OOM count, segmented by selected profile.

Marcus Reed: cool. I’ll sync with Benji/Ethan on schema additions (grow_step_blocks).
